title: USB: CDC, HID, storage, host and device roles

spans.text: USB is more than power and a Serial Monitor cable. With the right chip and board, a microcontroller can appear as a computer peripheral or act as a host for devices.

As a device, USB can expose CDC serial diagnostics, HID input, MSC storage, MIDI, or supported DFU updates. As a host, it manages keyboards, mice, and storage; the host must provide 5 V VBUS and suitable current. ESP32-S2/S3 have USB OTG for host/device roles, subject to board wiring and Arduino USB Mode settings; S3 USB Serial/JTAG and OTG can share a PHY. C3 has native CDC/JTAG but not full USB host OTG. The original ESP32 has no native USB peripheral. An UNO's USB connector normally leads to a USB-UART bridge, so it cannot act as a standard USB keyboard. ATmega32U4 and suitable ESP32-S2/S3 boards can provide native HID.

In the sample, `Serial` maps to native CDC on some boards and to UART through a USB-UART bridge on others; check IDE options and the board schematic.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Check the board's VBUS power circuit for USB host use; never power peripherals from a GPIO pin. HID key events must be tied to clear, authorized user action.
